```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse, knitr, patchwork, conflicted)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, dplyr::select, dplyr::mutate, dplyr::summarise, here::here)

TAB <- here("outputs", "tables", "backdating")
FIG <- here("outputs", "figures", "backdating")
ONSET_MIN <- 2000L; ONSET_MAX <- 2017L          # = build_04_backdating.R
LT_MAG <- 200; LT_DUR <- 4; LT_PRE <- 100       # = build_04_backdating.R

f <- function(...) file.path(TAB, ...)
pending <- function(what) cat(sprintf("\n> **Pending:** %s\n\n", what))
first_existing <- function(paths) { p <- paths[file.exists(paths)]; if (length(p)) p[1] else NA_character_ }

# --- accuracy helpers (pixel- or point-weighted) ---
acc <- function(onset, truth, w = rep(1, length(truth))) {
  dated <- !is.na(onset); e <- (onset - truth)[dated]; wd <- w[dated]
  tibble(coverage = 100 * sum(wd) / sum(w),
         exact = 100 * sum(wd[e == 0]) / sum(wd),
         pm1   = 100 * sum(wd[abs(e) <= 1]) / sum(wd),
         pm2   = 100 * sum(wd[abs(e) <= 2]) / sum(wd),
         pm1_of_all = 100 * sum(wd[abs(e) <= 1]) / sum(w),
         mean_error = sum(wd * e) / sum(wd))
}
fmt_acc <- function(x) x |> mutate(across(c(coverage, exact, pm1, pm2, pm1_of_all), ~ round(.x, 1)),
                                   mean_error = round(mean_error, 2))
acc_cols <- c("dated (%)", "exact (%)", "±1 yr (%)", "±2 yr (%)", "±1 yr, share of all (%)", "mean error (yr)")
# Naming rule: "Barenblitt replica" = OUR implementation of their method; "Barenblitt et al." = their data.
mlab <- c(barenblitt = "Barenblitt replica (ours)", landtrendr = "LandTrendr", ccdc = "CCDC")

# --- embeddings ground-truth test: v2 (3 methods, dense + thinned) preferred over v1 (dense, 2 methods) ---
# *_ccdc = the 3-method run; *_e = the rule-e test (2 methods, read separately), never picked here
v2_path <- first_existing(c(list.files(TAB, "groundtruth_v2_bar_hull.*_ccdc\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE),
                            list.files(TAB, "groundtruth_v2_.*_ccdc\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)))
v1_path <- first_existing(f("validate_backdating_vs_classifier_groundtruth_bar_hull.csv"))
gt <- if (!is.na(v2_path)) {
  read_csv(v2_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    rename(any_of(c(barenblitt = "bar", landtrendr = "lt", ccdc = "cc"))) |>
    pivot_longer(any_of(c("barenblitt", "landtrendr", "ccdc")), names_to = "method", values_to = "onset")
} else if (!is.na(v1_path)) {
  read_csv(v1_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(imagery = "full") |>
    rename(barenblitt = onset_bar, landtrendr = onset_lt) |>
    pivot_longer(c(barenblitt, landtrendr), names_to = "method", values_to = "onset")
} else NULL
gt_src <- if (!is.na(v2_path)) basename(v2_path) else if (!is.na(v1_path)) basename(v1_path) else NA
gt_is_v1 <- is.na(v2_path) && !is.na(v1_path)
gt_score <- function(x) x |> group_by(method, imagery) |>
  reframe(acc(onset, first_detected_year, n_pixels)) |> fmt_acc()

# --- Barenblitt classifica comparison: all three methods on Barenblitt's own 2019 footprint ---
# (validate_backdating_method_fidelity.R). Their labels run one year earlier than ours, so
# classifica + 1 is the comparable year; that script's window runs to 2018 for this reason.
fid_path <- first_existing(f("validate_backdating_fidelity_3methods.csv"))
```

```{r summary-numbers, include=FALSE}
gt_persist <- if (!is.null(gt)) gt_score(filter(gt, persistent == 1)) else NULL
bar_dense  <- if (!is.null(gt_persist)) filter(gt_persist, method == "barenblitt", imagery == "full") else NULL
```

# Summary

**What this is.** We want to know when mining began on land that is mined today. The embeddings
classifier maps mining only from 2017 on. So we take every pixel mined in its 2017 mask, look back
through the Landsat archive (1998-2018) for the year its vegetation was cleared, and impute that as
the pixel's conversion year ("onset"). Joined with the classifier's first detections from 2018, this
gives one onset series for 2000-2025, which feeds the panel.

```{r bottom-line, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(bar_dense)) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "- **Method:** the Barenblitt-replica NDVI method (Section 1) dates every pixel mined by 2017 to an onset year, %d-%d.\n",
    "- **When imagery is good, it finds the right year:** %.0f%% of reliable pixels are dated within ±1 year of ",
    "the year the embeddings classifier first detects them, with no systematic offset (mean error %+.2f yr).\n"),
    ONSET_MIN, ONSET_MAX, bar_dense$pm1, bar_dense$mean_error))
} else pending("embeddings ground-truth test")
thin <- if (!is.null(gt_persist)) filter(gt_persist, method == "barenblitt", imagery == "thin") else NULL
if (!is.null(thin) && nrow(thin)) {
  cat(sprintf("- **With imagery thinned to pre-2013 sparsity:** %.0f%% within ±1 year (dated: %.0f%%).\n", thin$pm1, thin$coverage))
} else cat("- **With sparse, pre-2013-like imagery:** pending (thinning test).\n")
cat("- **Why this method:** it dates nearly every pixel, which the panel needs. LandTrendr is precise where it fires but",
    "dates only a minority of pixels, so it serves as a confidence flag (`lt_agree`). CCDC: see Sections 2.2 and 3.\n")
cat("- **Weak spots, flagged rather than removed:** pixels already bare in 1998-2002, sparse early years, the 2002 pile-up",
    "and 2008. The panel collapses all onsets before 2005 into a starting stock.\n")
```

# 1. Methods

Dating a land-cover change from a satellite time series is a standard problem in earth observation,
and there are several ways to do it. We compare three: two widely used general-purpose
change-detection algorithms, **LandTrendr** and **CCDC**, and the method **Barenblitt et al. (2021)**
used to date galamsey in south-west Ghana. All three look for the break in a pixel's vegetation
record. They differ in how much imagery they need and in whether they always return a year.

- **LandTrendr** (Kennedy et al., 2010). Reduces each year to one value (here median NBR), fits a
  piecewise-linear trajectory through the years, and takes the start of the largest loss segment.
  The loss counts only if it passes size, duration and starting-vegetation thresholds (we use
  Barenblitt et al.'s: magnitude > 200, duration < 4 yr, pre-value > 100).
  *Needs:* about one clear observation per year. *Pro:* robust to noisy single observations, and
  tells abrupt clearing apart from slow decline. *Con:* the thresholds leave most pixels undated,
  because gradual or partial losses on already-degraded land fail them (Section 2).
- **CCDC** (Zhu & Woodcock, 2014). Uses every clear observation: it fits a seasonal model (harmonics
  plus trend) to each pixel and flags a break when consecutive observations stray from the model's
  prediction (settings as Barenblitt et al.: minimum 3 observations, chi-square 0.8). Onset = the
  break with the largest NDVI drop. *Needs:* dense imagery, several clear observations per year, to
  fit the seasonal cycle and confirm a break. *Pro:* uses all the data and dates breaks within the
  year. *Con:* too data-hungry for the early record. With recent imagery thinned to pre-2013
  density, the share of pixels it dates collapses (Section 2.2).
- **Barenblitt method** (Barenblitt et al., 2021). Takes each year's greenest NDVI value, smooths
  it over 3 years, and picks the year of the largest drop (details in 1.1).
  *Needs:* at least one clear observation in each of four consecutive years. *Pro:* dates nearly
  every pixel, it is simple, and it produced the only existing galamsey onset data, so ours is
  directly comparable. *Con:* there is no minimum loss, so it always picks a year, even where
  nothing much happened. It is sensitive to changes in how many observations a year has (the 2002
  pile-up, Section 4), and the smoothing spreads a sharp loss over neighbouring years.

We deploy the Barenblitt method and keep LandTrendr as a confidence flag (`lt_agree`); Section 3
sets out why. **Naming:** "Barenblitt replica" means our implementation of their method;
"Barenblitt et al." means their published data.

## 1.1 The imagery: Landsat 1998-2018

All three methods date the loss from the Landsat archive, and how much imagery it holds decides
which method can work. Before 2013 a mined pixel has about 1-3 clear observations per year; from
2015 about 10. The satellites explain why. Landsat 5 was in orbit throughout, but recorded little
over West Africa in the 2000s. Landsat 7 lost its scan-line corrector in May 2003, so every later
scene has striped gaps. Only Landsat 8 (from 2013) brought full, regular coverage. Landsat 6 never
reached orbit (1993), and Landsat 9 (2021) is after our window.

```{r scene-cov, fig.height=4.2, fig.width=8}
sc <- read_csv(f("scene_coverage_anchor2017.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
# Year y is drawn from y - 0.5 to y + 0.5, so a date (decimal year d) sits at d - 0.5 on the same axis.
XL <- c(1997.5, 2018.5)
missions <- tribble(
  ~sensor,          ~status,                         ~from,   ~to,
  "Landsat 5 (TM)",   "operating (sparse over Ghana)", 1997.5, 2011.87 - 0.5,   # imaging ended Nov 2011
  "Landsat 7 (ETM+)", "full scenes",                   1999.29 - 0.5, 2003.41 - 0.5,   # launched Apr 1999
  "Landsat 7 (ETM+)", "scan-line gaps (SLC-off)",      2003.41 - 0.5, 2018.5,          # SLC failure 31 May 2003
  "Landsat 8 (OLI)",  "full scenes",                   2013.28 - 0.5, 2018.5           # data from Apr 2013
) |> mutate(sensor = factor(sensor, rev(c("Landsat 5 (TM)", "Landsat 7 (ETM+)", "Landsat 8 (OLI)"))))

p_sat <- ggplot(missions, aes(y = sensor)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = from, xend = to, yend = sensor, colour = status), linewidth = 5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`full scenes` = "#2a78d6", `scan-line gaps (SLC-off)` = "#eda100",
                                 `operating (sparse over Ghana)` = "#9ec5f4"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = XL, breaks = seq(2000, 2018, 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Landsat satellites in our imagery window") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank())

p_obs <- ggplot(sc, aes(year, mean_n_obs)) + geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8", width = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = p10_n_obs), colour = "#D7301F", size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = XL, breaks = seq(2000, 2018, 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "clear obs per pixel-year", title = "Clear observations per mined pixel",
       caption = "bars = mean, red dots = 10th percentile (pixels mined by 2017)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

p_sat / p_obs + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1, 2))
```

## 1.2 The Barenblitt method in detail

For every pixel mined by 2017 (from the embeddings classifier's 2017 mask):

1. Take every clear Landsat observation 1998-2018 and keep each year's **maximum NDVI**.
2. Smooth with a **3-year centred moving average**.
3. Compute the **year-on-year loss** in that average.
4. The year with the **largest loss** is the onset year.

There is no minimum size of loss: every pixel gets a year. A year can only be scored if the pixel has
clear observations in four consecutive years around it, so sparse early years limit which years
can win. A clean forest-to-bare step shows up as equal losses in three consecutive years (from the
smoothing). Our year label is the later one, which matches when the classifier first sees the mine
(Section 2). Barenblitt et al. label the same loss one year earlier.

Two example pixels: a clean loss, where the largest bar is unambiguous, and a gradual loss, where
the smoothing spreads the loss over several bars. The second is why accuracy is judged within ±1 year.
Weak cases follow in Section 4.

```{r mechanism-fig, out.width='100%'}
# ndvi_timeseries_method.png = 2-panel version (diag_04_backdating.R, 2026-11-16); the 10-panel
# ndvi_timeseries_examples.png is only a fallback until diag_04 is re-run on the current asset.
p <- first_existing(file.path(FIG, c("ndvi_timeseries_method.png", "ndvi_timeseries_examples.png")))
if (!is.na(p)) include_graphics(p) else pending("example-pixel figure (`diag_04_backdating.R`)")
```

# 2. Does it find the right year?

Apart from checking pixels by hand in historical imagery (not done yet), there are two ways to
judge the methods, each with a caveat:

1. **Against the classifier's own 2018-2025 conversions** (2.1, 2.2). Pixels the embeddings
   classifier first maps as mined in 2018-2025 have a known conversion year, independent of
   vegetation indices. But that year is the classifier's first detection, not the true conversion
   year, and recent imagery is far denser than the early record. 2.2 therefore repeats the test
   with the imagery thinned to pre-2013 density.
2. **Against Barenblitt et al.'s published conversion years** (`classifica`, 2007-2017; 2.3). These
   cover the real historical imagery, but they come from the same NDVI method the Barenblitt
   replica copies, so the comparison is tilted in its favour.

## 2.1 Against the classifier's 2018-2025 conversions

**Test:** pixels that first appear as mined in the embeddings classifier's masks in 2018-2025
(and were not mined in 2017) get that first-detection year as a reference. Every method is then
run on 2016-2026 Landsat imagery for the same pixels. *Persistent* pixels never drop out of the
masks after first detection; their reference year is the most reliable.

```{r gt-dense, results='asis'}
if (is.null(gt)) pending("embeddings ground-truth test") else {
  cat(sprintf("Source: `%s`, %s pixels (%.0f km²).%s\n\n", gt_src,
              format(round(sum(gt$n_pixels[gt$method == "barenblitt" & gt$imagery == "full"])), big.mark = ","),
              sum(gt$n_pixels[gt$method == "barenblitt" & gt$imagery == "full"]) * 900 / 1e6,
              if (gt_is_v1) " LandTrendr here uses the **old** single-year gate (>100), not the deployed 200/4/100 version." else ""))
  bind_rows(gt_score(filter(gt, persistent == 1, imagery == "full")) |> mutate(pixels = "persistent"),
            gt_score(filter(gt, imagery == "full")) |> mutate(pixels = "all")) |>
    mutate(method = mlab[method]) |>
    select(pixels, method, coverage:mean_error) |>
    kable(col.names = c("pixels", "method", acc_cols)) |> print()
}
```

```{r gt-signed, fig.height=3.2, fig.width=8}
if (!is.null(gt)) {
  gt |> filter(persistent == 1, imagery == "full", !is.na(onset)) |>
    mutate(diff = pmax(pmin(onset - first_detected_year, 4), -4)) |>
    group_by(method, diff) |> summarise(px = sum(n_pixels), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(method) |> mutate(pct = 100 * px / sum(px)) |> ungroup() |> mutate(method = mlab[method]) |>
    ggplot(aes(diff, pct)) + geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8") + facet_wrap(~ method) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = -4:4, labels = c("≤-4", -3:3, "≥4")) +
    labs(x = "method year minus first-detection year", y = "% of dated persistent pixels") +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

**Reading it:** a peak at 0 means the year label lines up with when the classifier first sees
the mine, so the backdated era (to 2017) and the embeddings era (2018 on) mean the same thing at
the seam. This is a **best case** for imagery: 2018-2025 has about 10 clear observations per pixel
per year, against 1-3 before 2013.

## 2.2 The same test with sparse imagery

The same test, with each pixel's 2016-2026 imagery randomly thinned to about 2.5 clear observations
per year, the pre-2013 average (some years end up with none, as in the early record). The gaps are
random, whereas real early gaps cluster in the wet season.

```{r gt-thin-bars, fig.height=3, fig.width=8}
if (!is.null(gt) && "thin" %in% gt$imagery) {
  gt_score(filter(gt, persistent == 1)) |>
    select(method, imagery, `dated` = coverage, `dated and within ±1 yr` = pm1_of_all) |>
    pivot_longer(-c(method, imagery), names_to = "measure", values_to = "pct") |>
    mutate(method = factor(mlab[method], mlab),
           imagery = factor(imagery, c("full", "thin"), c("dense (2016-2026 as is)", "thinned to pre-2013 density"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(method, pct, fill = imagery)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(pct)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ measure) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834"), name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 105), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of all persistent pixels") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
}
```

```{r gt-thin, results='asis'}
if (is.null(gt) || !"thin" %in% gt$imagery) pending("thinning test (`validate_backdating_vs_classifier_groundtruth.R` with `THIN_TARGET = 2.5`)") else {
  gt_score(filter(gt, persistent == 1)) |> arrange(method, imagery) |>
    mutate(method = mlab[method]) |>
    select(method, imagery, coverage:mean_error) |>
    kable(col.names = c("method", "imagery", acc_cols), caption = "Persistent pixels, dense vs thinned") |> print()
}
```

## 2.3 Against Barenblitt et al.'s conversion years

All three methods are run on the real historical imagery, on Barenblitt et al.'s own mapped
footprint, so every one of their points can be scored and differences in what counts as "mined"
don't enter. Their years are shifted +1 to match our label convention (Section 1.2). Part of the
Barenblitt replica's agreement is mechanical, since it copies the method behind these years.

```{r cls-compare, results='asis'}
if (is.na(fid_path)) pending("three-method classifica comparison (`validate_backdating_method_fidelity.R`)") else {
  d <- read_csv(fid_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(truth = 2001L + as.integer(classifica)) |>
    pivot_longer(c(onset_bar, onset_lt, onset_cc), names_to = "method", values_to = "onset") |>
    mutate(method = recode(method, onset_bar = "barenblitt", onset_lt = "landtrendr", onset_cc = "ccdc"),
           onset = if_else(onset == 0, NA_real_, as.numeric(onset)))
  d |> group_by(method) |> reframe(acc(onset, truth), points = n()) |> fmt_acc() |>
    mutate(method = mlab[method]) |>
    select(method, points, coverage:mean_error) |>
    kable(col.names = c("method", "points", acc_cols),
          caption = "Barenblitt et al.'s classifica points (+1 yr) on their own 2019 footprint, 2007-2018 window") |> print()
}
```

```{r cls-signed, fig.height=3, fig.width=8}
if (!is.na(fid_path)) {
  d |> filter(!is.na(onset)) |> mutate(diff = pmax(pmin(onset - truth, 4), -4)) |>
    count(method, diff) |> group_by(method) |> mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |> ungroup() |>
    mutate(method = mlab[method]) |>
    ggplot(aes(diff, pct)) + geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8") + facet_wrap(~ method) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = -4:4, labels = c("≤-4", -3:3, "≥4")) +
    labs(x = "method year minus (Barenblitt et al. year + 1)", y = "% of dated points") + theme_minimal()
}
```

# 3. Why the Barenblitt-replica method?

The panel needs an onset year for nearly every mined pixel, so coverage matters as much as accuracy
among dated pixels. The column "±1 yr, share of all" in the tables above combines the two.

# 4. What the backdating shows, and its weak spots

```{r results-data}
sum_path <- f(sprintf("onset_summary_%d_%d.csv", ONSET_MIN, ONSET_MAX))
osum <- if (file.exists(sum_path)) read_csv(sum_path, show_col_types = FALSE) else NULL
bar_area <- if (file.exists(f("barenblitt_yearly_area.csv"))) read_csv(f("barenblitt_yearly_area.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) else NULL
```

```{r results-headline, results='asis'}
                     "**%.1f%%** could not be dated. **%.0f%%** are dated before 2005 and form the panel's starting stock.\n\n"),
              format(round(tot), big.mark = ","), tot * 900 / 1e6,
              100 * sum(osum$n_pixels[osum$region == "bar_hull"]) / tot, 100 * und / tot, 100 * pre05 / tot))
```

```{r results-area, fig.height=3.6, fig.width=8}
  osum |> filter(onset_year > 0) |> group_by(onset_year, region) |>
    summarise(km2 = sum(n_pixels) * 900 / 1e6, .groups = "drop") |>

    geom_vline(xintercept = 2004.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    annotate("text", x = 2004.4, y = Inf, label = "panel: before 2005 = starting stock", hjust = 1, vjust = 1.5, size = 3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(bar_hull = "#2C7FB8", outside = "#FDB863"),
                      labels = c(bar_hull = "Barenblitt et al. study area", outside = "rest of Ghana")) +
    labs(x = "onset year", y = "new mining area (km²)", fill = NULL) + theme_minimal()
}
```

## 4.1 Our series against Barenblitt et al.'s data

```{r series-data}
cls <- if (file.exists(f("classifier_era_area_2017_2025.csv"))) read_csv(f("classifier_era_area_2017_2025.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) else NULL
# One continuous onset series per region: backdated 2000-2017 (undatable pixels added at 2017, they are
# in the 2017 mask) + classifier first detections 2018-2025.
onset_series <- function(reg) {
  if (is.null(osum) || is.null(cls)) return(NULL)
  o <- osum |> filter(region %in% reg)
  back <- o |> filter(onset_year > 0) |> group_by(year = onset_year) |>
    summarise(new_km2 = sum(n_pixels) * 900 / 1e6, .groups = "drop") |> mutate(source = "backdated (Barenblitt replica, Landsat)")
  und  <- tibble(year = ONSET_MAX, new_km2 = sum(o$n_pixels[o$onset_year == 0]) * 900 / 1e6, source = "undatable (in 2017 mask)")
  new  <- cls |> filter(region %in% reg, year > ONSET_MAX) |> group_by(year) |>
    summarise(new_km2 = sum(new_km2), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(source = "classifier (first detection)")
  bind_rows(back, und, new) |> arrange(year)
}
ours_bh <- onset_series("bar_hull")
ours_gh <- onset_series(c("bar_hull", "outside"))
theirs  <- if (!is.null(bar_area)) bar_area |> transmute(year = bar_year + 1L, new_km2 = bar_km2) else NULL
```

```{r series-pending, results='asis'}
if (is.null(cls)) pending("classifier-era series (`diag_04_backdating.R`, Section 2c)")
```

Both series count **new** mining area per year inside Barenblitt et al.'s study area, from 2008 (their
first year, shifted +1 to our label convention) to 2018. Ours is the backdated product to 2017 and the
classifier's first detections in 2018. The levels differ because the footprints differ (ours: everything
the classifier maps as mined; theirs: their own map), so the shape over time is what to compare.

```{r series-vs-barenblitt, fig.height=3.4, fig.width=9}
if (!is.null(ours_bh) && !is.null(theirs)) {
  cmp <- bind_rows(
    ours_bh |> group_by(year) |> summarise(new_km2 = sum(new_km2), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(series = "ours (Barenblitt replica + classifier)"),
    theirs |> mutate(series = "Barenblitt et al. data (+1 yr)")) |>
    filter(year >= 2008, year <= 2018) |>
    group_by(series) |> arrange(year) |> mutate(cum_km2 = cumsum(new_km2)) |> ungroup() |>
    pivot_longer(c(new_km2, cum_km2), names_to = "measure", values_to = "km2") |>
    mutate(measure = factor(measure, c("new_km2", "cum_km2"), c("new area per year", "cumulative since 2008")))
  ggplot(cmp, aes(year, km2, colour = series)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`ours (Barenblitt replica + classifier)` = "#2C7FB8", `Barenblitt et al. data (+1 yr)` = "#D7301F")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2008, 2018, 2)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "km²", colour = NULL) + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

```{r series-corr, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(ours_bh) && !is.null(theirs)) {
  j <- inner_join(ours_bh |> group_by(year) |> summarise(ours = sum(new_km2), .groups = "drop"),
                  theirs |> rename(bar = new_km2), by = "year") |> filter(year >= 2008, year <= 2018)
  cat(sprintf("Correlation of new area per year, 2008-2018: r = %.2f (cumulative: r = %.2f).\n\n",
              cor(j$ours, j$bar), cor(cumsum(j$ours), cumsum(j$bar))))
}
```

## 4.2 The full series, 2000-2025

The backdated product (to 2017) joined with the classifier's first detections (2018-2025). Bars are new
area per year by source; the line is the cumulative total. Points show the area each year's classifier
mask flags as mined: masks can flicker, so this stock is not cumulative and can sit below the line.
Before 2005 is collapsed into a starting stock in the panel.

```{r series-full, fig.height=6.5, fig.width=9}
if (!is.null(ours_gh)) {
  full <- bind_rows(ours_bh |> mutate(region = "Barenblitt et al. study area"), ours_gh |> mutate(region = "All of Ghana"))
  cumline <- full |> group_by(region, year) |> summarise(new_km2 = sum(new_km2), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(region) |> arrange(year) |> mutate(cum_km2 = cumsum(new_km2)) |> ungroup()
  stock <- bind_rows(cls |> filter(region == "bar_hull") |> mutate(region = "Barenblitt et al. study area"),
                     cls |> group_by(year) |> summarise(stock_km2 = sum(stock_km2), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(region = "All of Ghana")) |>
    select(region, year, stock_km2)
  sc_f <- max(cumline$cum_km2) / max(full$new_km2)   # second axis scale
  ggplot() +
    geom_col(data = full, aes(year, new_km2 * sc_f, fill = source), width = 0.8) +
    geom_line(data = cumline, aes(year, cum_km2), linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(data = stock, aes(year, stock_km2), shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(2004.5, 2017.5), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    facet_wrap(~ region, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_y_continuous(name = "cumulative mined area (km², line)",
                       sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / sc_f, name = "new area per year (km², bars)")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`backdated (Barenblitt replica, Landsat)` = "#2C7FB8", `undatable (in 2017 mask)` = "grey60",
                                 `classifier (first detection)` = "#FDB863")) +
    labs(x = NULL, fill = NULL) + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

```{r series-seam, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(ours_gh)) {
  s17 <- sum(cls$stock_km2[cls$year == 2017])
  b17 <- sum(ours_gh$new_km2[ours_gh$year <= 2017])
  cat(sprintf(paste0("**Seam check:** cumulative backdated area through 2017 = %.0f km², the 2017 classifier mask = %.0f km² ",
                     "(%.1f%% apart; both come from the same mask, on slightly different 30 m grids).\n"),
              b17, s17, 100 * (b17 - s17) / s17))
}
```

```{r results-flags}
if (!is.null(osum)) {
  osum |> filter(onset_year > 0) |> group_by(onset_year) |>
    summarise(km2 = sum(n_pixels) * 900 / 1e6,
              agree_pct = 100 * sum(n_pixels[lt_agree == "agree"]) / sum(n_pixels),   # new names: reusing lt_agree here would overwrite the column
              disagree_pct = 100 * sum(n_pixels[lt_agree == "disagree"]) / sum(n_pixels),
              bare_start = 100 * sum(n_pixels[start_class == "bare"]) / sum(n_pixels),
              small_loss = 100 * sum(n_pixels[deriv_x1000 < 100]) / sum(n_pixels),
              mean_computable = sum(n_pixels * n_computable) / sum(n_pixels), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(across(-onset_year, ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
    kable(col.names = c("onset year", "km²", "LandTrendr agrees (%)", "LandTrendr disagrees (%)",
                        "bare in 1998-2002 (%)", "small loss <100 (%)", "mean computable years"),
          caption = "Confidence flags by onset year, all of Ghana. Loss is ×1000 on the 3-yr average; 100 ≈ a sustained raw NDVI drop of 0.3.")
}
```

**Weak spots, by example.** Most weak spots trace back to the sparse early imagery (Section 1.1).
Three example pixels: a one-year dip (a single low observation creates a false onset, the cause of
the 2002 pile-up), a pixel that was already bare at the start (no real loss to find), and a pixel
dated years before Barenblitt et al.'s year.

```{r weakspots-fig, out.width='100%'}
p <- file.path(FIG, "ndvi_timeseries_weakspots.png")
if (file.exists(p)) include_graphics(p) else pending("weak-spots figure (`diag_04_backdating.R`, regenerated from the asset)")
```

| Weak spot | What we see | How it's handled |
|---|---|---|
| Already bare in 1998-2002 | 3% of dated pixels; smaller losses; real onset may predate the series | flag `start_ndvi_x1000`; optionally counted as "before 2005" |
| Few computable years | some pixels choose from only a handful of candidate years | flag `n_computable_years`, `n_obs_years` |
| 2002 pile-up | 7.4% of onsets (0.5% in 2001). Mostly one low observation in 2003, the first Landsat 7 SLC-off year, with NDVI back to normal the next year (`diag_06_onset_2002_check.R`). The same one-year dips make up 40-60% of all onsets before 2012 | under test: interpolating single-observation years (rule e) |
| 2008 (and 2009) | few pixels, more bare at start, smaller losses; Barenblitt et al.'s data often date these much later | see the LandTrendr columns in the flags table above |
| Smaller losses before 2011 | sparser imagery or more gradual early clearing | no minimum-loss threshold: it would cut early years far more and make mining look later |


# 5. Settings and why

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor footprint | embeddings mask, mined by 2017 | 2018+ onsets come from the classifier directly |
| Onset window | 2000-2017 | 2017 was cut off before (8.9% "undatable"); the panel reports pre-2005 as one stock |
| Imagery | 1998-2018, full year | the 3-yr average needs a year either side; shortening it would misdate early mining |
| Year label | later year of the loss | matches the classifier's first detection (Section 2) |
| Minimum loss | none | no natural cut-off; a threshold biases the timeline |
| LandTrendr (cross-check) | mag > 200, dur < 4, pre-value > 100 | Barenblitt et al.'s comparison settings |

# Appendix: deployed asset bands

`mine_onset_year_2000_2017_barenblitt`, 30 m:

| Band | Meaning | No-data value |
|---|---|---|
| `onset_year` | onset year | 0 = not datable |
| `ndvi_deriv_x1000` | size of the winning loss, ×1000 | -9999 |
| `reference_tier` | 0 = onset before 2007, 1 = 2007+ (comparable with Barenblitt et al.'s years) | 9 |
| `lt_agree` | 0 LandTrendr agrees ±2 yr, 1 disagrees, 2 no LandTrendr signal | 9 |
| `n_obs_years` | years 1998-2018 with ≥1 clear observation | – |
| `n_computable_years` | candidate years that could be scored | – |
| `start_ndvi_x1000` | median annual max NDVI 1998-2002, ×1000 | -9999 |
